chapters.title: Why you're still in it
chapters.teaser: The real reason your soul keeps saying 'let's see where it goes'.

chapters.title: What you actually want
chapters.teaser: Not what sounds chill. What you'd ask for if you weren't worried.

chapters.title: How you read mixed signals
chapters.teaser: Your decoding habit, and a better way to get information.

chapters.title: The talk, your way
chapters.teaser: How to ask 'what are we' in words that fit your soul.

chapters.title: Your line
chapters.teaser: The one thing you shouldn't keep accepting.

chapters.title: Either way, you're okay
chapters.teaser: What comes next, whatever answer you get.

text.why-you-stay: Mu Earth is the mountain: patient, steady, slow to move. In a situationship you wait. You assume things will settle into a shape if you just keep being reliable. At first you may not even mind the low pressure, since it asks nothing dramatic of you. You stay because leaving would require a decision you haven't fully made, and because you're loyal even to things without a name. Ask yourself one practical question: am I waiting for something specific to happen, or am I just waiting because waiting is what I do?
text.what-you-want: You want stability, someone you can actually count on. Mu Earth rarely says that out loud, because you'd rather show it than ask for it. You show up, you keep your word, you remember things. But being reliable yourself doesn't automatically make the other person reliable back. Name your want plainly: consistent plans, exclusivity, someone who shows up when it matters and not only when it's convenient. If that isn't happening, more patience from you is not the fix. It's simply more of the same. Wanting it doesn't make you demanding. It makes you clear about the foundation you'd build on.
text.mixed-signals: When signals are mixed, you tend to ignore them and hold your course. Mu Earth is very good at not reacting, which keeps you calm and steady. It also means you could sit for months in something that never actually moved. Instead of waiting for one clear signal, look at the pattern over time. Has anything grown, deepened, or become more defined since the first month? Are you meeting their friends, making plans further ahead? Mountains notice erosion slowly. Check the landscape honestly. If the honest answer is nothing has changed, then the stillness is the signal, and you can stop waiting for a louder one.
text.the-talk: Your talk can be straightforward, almost practical, and that suits you well. Pick a calm moment, maybe a walk where you're side by side. Say: I like what we have, and I'd like it to be more defined. Where are you at? Mu Earth's risk is saying it so neutrally that they don't realise it matters to you at all. So add one honest sentence on top: this matters to me. Then listen properly, without deciding in advance what their answer means or how you'll react. Afterward, give yourself a day before deciding anything. You process best slowly, and that's allowed.
text.your-line: Your line is being taken for granted. Mountains are reliable, and people lean on them without thinking about it. If you're always the available one, the one who adjusts plans, the one with no real say in what this is, notice that pattern. Decide what effort you need in return, in concrete terms. When it's missing week after week, step away calmly and without drama. Mountains don't chase. They don't have to. The right people climb toward them on purpose. Write down two or three concrete examples of effort you'd expect. If you can't remember the last time you saw one, that tells you plenty about where things stand.
text.either-way: Either way, you'll stand. If they want more, it will be built on something solid, because you are solid. If not, you'll take some time, probably more than you show anyone, and then you'll move forward with your usual quiet strength. Let one friend know how you're actually doing, in honest words rather than I'm fine. Even mountains need company sometimes. You've been the steady thing for other people for so long. Let someone be steady for you for a week. Then shift one small thing in your week, a new route or a new class, so your life feels like it's moving too.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You've been so patient and steady, Mu.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Patient, or just not deciding? Be honest.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Wanting stability is reasonable.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Then say 'this matters to me'. Out loud. With your mouth.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Look at the pattern, not one good night.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Has anything moved since month one? Check the map.

spring.intro: Spring roots push through the mountain, and Wood commanded your birth season, Mu. Wood controls Earth, which gave you patience under pressure and a habit of letting other people's needs grow through you. In a situationship you've probably become wonderfully accommodating. Their schedule, their pace, their uncertainty. You don't complain, you hold steady. And it works, for them. Spring Mu's blind spot is forgetting that a mountain is allowed to have terms. You're not difficult for wanting to know what this is. Name one thing you need, a plan, a label, a weekend, and see whether they make room.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Being endlessly accommodating isn't a love language, Mu. It's a rental agreement.

summer.intro: A summer mountain is solid and sun-warmed. Fire ruled your season, Mu, and Fire generates Earth, so you have a steady confidence most people envy. In a situationship that makes you look unbothered. You're happy to keep showing up, reliable as ever. But steady can also mean stuck. You might stay in this simply because leaving would require movement, and mountains don't love moving. Summer Mu's honest question isn't whether they'll commit. It's whether you're still here by choice or by inertia. You can feel secure and still want more. Wanting more is not instability.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Feeling secure and wanting more can both be true, Mu.

autumn.intro: Autumn Mu gives freely, the way a mountain gives up ore. Metal ruled your birth season and Earth produces Metal, so you show care through practical help: driving them places, fixing their laptop, being the dependable one. In a situationship you've likely become indispensable without becoming official. They lean on you. They don't label you. The autumn blind spot is believing usefulness will eventually be rewarded with commitment. Sometimes it is. Often it just gets used. Watch what happens when you stop solving things for a while. A partner shows up for you too. A situationship mostly shows up when it needs something.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You fixed their laptop, moved their sofa, still no label. Interesting pattern, Mu.

winter.intro: Winter Mu is the dam holding back a frozen river. Water ruled your birth season, and Earth controls Water, so you're excellent at containing feelings: yours, theirs, everyone's. In a situationship that means you keep it calm. No drama, no demands, no messy questions. You manage the emotional temperature so well that nobody, including you, notices how much you want. The winter blind spot is control that slowly becomes silence. Let one feeling out without managing it first. Tell them you'd like more. The river won't flood the valley. It'll just show both of you what's actually been building.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your feelings aren't a flood risk, Mu. Let one out and see.

strength.strong: Your mountain stands on solid ground, Mu, so you're steady, secure and slow to change course. In a situationship you might be comfortable enough never to push. Or you've decided what this is in your head and act as if it's settled, without checking with them. The blind spot of strong Earth is assuming that because you're sure, they are too. Ask out loud. A mountain that never speaks can't be surprised, but it also can't be met halfway. Steady and talkative can live in the same person.
strength.weak: With thin support in your chart, Mu, you hold steady by sheer effort. In a situationship you might be absorbing every bit of their uncertainty and calling it patience. You keep being reliable for someone who isn't reliable back. The blind spot is believing that if you stay solid long enough, they'll settle on you. Solid ground can be walked on forever without anyone buying it. Your needs count as much as your patience. Tell them what you want, and decide privately how long you're willing to wait.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and definition. In a situationship you might rush clarity, or picture a whole future before the other person has caught up to the present. Your drive is a good thing. Just give them room to answer at their own pace once you've asked. Ask once, clearly, then step back and let the answer come. Balance with a little Metal: clear boundaries, finished business, knowing when something needs pruning rather than more growth.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means starting things, including the talk, feels hard. You might let an undefined situation drift on and on simply because initiating anything feels heavy. Build momentum in small steps: decide what you want, write it down, choose a day to ask. Spend time outdoors and around green things. You don't need to grow everything at once. You only need one honest question, asked once, out loud.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire means big feelings, fast. In a situationship you might swing between excitement and frustration in the same evening, and want answers right now. Slow your pace a little. Pick a calm moment for the talk, not a heated one. Cool down with water: rest, quiet nights in, a walk before sending any big message. Your passion is attractive. Just don't let it make your decisions at midnight.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means expressing feelings and being seen can feel hard. You might keep this situationship low-key so that nobody, including you, has to admit it matters. Turn the light up a little. Let your feelings show in small ways. Be visible in your own life too: plans, friends, sunlight, music. The more you shine for yourself, the easier the honest question becomes when you finally ask it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you wait, stay steady, and stay put, sometimes for too long. In a situationship you may tolerate a lack of definition because change feels disruptive and messy. Bring in a bit of movement: pick a day by which you'll have the talk, and keep it. Let some Wood in, growth and fresh starts. Stable doesn't have to mean stuck, and patient doesn't have to mean silent.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means stability is hard to find, and an undefined relationship can make you feel even more unsteady than usual. Ground yourself first: routines, regular meals, a dependable circle of friends. Then have the talk from a steady place, not a shaky one. You'll think more clearly and ask more clearly when your own ground is solid under your feet, whatever the answer turns out to be.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal means you want clarity and might cut too fast to get it. In a situationship you may issue ultimatums or go cold the moment things feel vague. Your boundaries are strong, which is good. Soften the delivery: ask with curiosity first, decide second. Water helps here: rest, reflection, letting a feeling be felt before you act on it.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard. In a situationship you may accept less than you want and keep telling yourself it's fine. Practise clear edges: decide your line and write it down somewhere you'll see it. Say no to plans that don't work for you. White and silver, decluttering, finishing things all support you. A boundary isn't harsh. It's honesty about what you need.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means overthinking and very deep feeling. In a situationship you might analyse every message and drown in what-ifs that never happen. Your intuition is valuable, but it needs a shore to land on. Earth helps: routines, physical activity, friends who ground you. Put a limit on the analysis. Ask the question instead of guessing the answer.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means reflection and rest get skipped. You might keep the situationship busy and fun so you never have to stop and think about what it actually is. Make space for quiet: a journal, a slow evening, a moment alone to ask yourself what you really want here. Clarity starts inside you before it's ever spoken to them, and it's worth the quiet.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you've planned your future together. They haven't planned Saturday.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy is lovely. Point it at what you want, not only at them.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: one great date and you're naming the dog. Breathe.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is magnetic. Let them match it before you double it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: you've waited so patiently you've basically become their furniture.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is a gift. It's fair to ask for steadiness back.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal: you've drafted an ultimatum. Maybe try a question first.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is strength. Soften the delivery and it lands beautifully.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you analysed one 'haha' with three friends and a tarot app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your sensitivity notices so much. Check the signals against actual actions too.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make it hard to picture what you want. Try imagining it.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no vision. You're seeing where it goes without looking anywhere.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make it hard to show interest. A little warmth helps.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. They genuinely cannot tell if you like them. Neither can I.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it easy to drift. Choose one thing you're sure about.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no ground. You change your mind about them every other day.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal can blur your line. You can decide what you won't accept.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means no line. You'll accept 'wyd' at midnight forever.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make feelings hard to say. Try writing them first.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. You'd rather move countries than say 'I like you.'

gap-wood.title: Pushing a mountain to see if it's interested
gap-wood.text: A Gap Wood wants to grow somewhere, and right now they're trying to grow towards you. That can feel flattering on Monday and exhausting by Thursday. The plans come in fast: a trip, a gig, meeting the friends, a new hobby you could take up together. You like them. You also like your Sunday exactly the way it is. So you say maybe, and reply when you've actually thought about it, which might be hours later. For you, that's respect. For Gap, it can look like a closed door. The signal you send is steadiness, but in a situationship steadiness without words reads as not interested. Gap also has a habit of trying to improve what they love, so you may feel lightly managed. You're allowed to say so. For the talk, Gap needs to hear your position out loud, not inferred from your silence. Even a short sentence does it: I like you. I move slowly, but I'm not going anywhere. I'd like this to be real. And if Gap's pace is too much, say that too, kindly and specifically. Mountains don't have to move. They do have to speak.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu's four-hour reply is sincere. It just arrives on mountain time.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap, stop renovating the mountain. It wasn't for sale.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, say it out loud once. Silence isn't a sentence.

eul-wood.title: Climbing the mountain the clever way
eul-wood.text: An Eul Wood climbs into your life gradually and then everywhere at once. Morning stickers, a voice note about their coworker, an invitation to a picnic with nine people you've never met. It's a lot, and it's also kind of lovely, the way ivy on a stone wall is lovely. You reply when you have something real to say, which is often hours later and two words long. To you, that's sincerity. To Eul, it can look like you're barely in it. The drift starts when Eul tries to read you. A vine looks for a way around a rock, so when you're quiet, Eul tries charm, then hints, then gently arranging things so you end up at the picnic. You notice, and you dig in, and suddenly a nice thing feels like a negotiation. Your signal is steadiness, but without words Eul can't see it. For the talk, you don't need a speech. You need one clear sentence and maybe a heart emoji, which costs you very little and means a lot to Eul: I'm not much of a texter, but I'm serious about you. I'd like us to be official. Then say it again in person, because a mountain's word carries more weight face to face.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, your 'ok' is warm. Eul just can't hear it from down here.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul, inviting their best friend so they have to come? Cute. Also sneaky.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Straight up the mountain. No clever route.

byeong-fire.title: Twelve messages, one sincere sentence
byeong-fire.text: A Byeong Fire walks into your quiet life like a festival. Suddenly there are plans, people, a night market, a trip to the seaside booked on a Tuesday. You enjoy more of it than you expected. You also need a whole Sunday afterwards to recover. The drift starts with how differently you both communicate. Byeong sends twelve messages; you send one, and you mean every word of it. Byeong might read your one as half-hearted. When Byeong is excited about something, you tend to respond with a calm 'sounds good', and to a sun, that lands like a cloud. And when there's tension, Byeong flares up and you go silent, which only makes Byeong flare more. Your signal is steadiness. Byeong may read it as not being impressed. For the talk, you don't need to match Byeong's energy. You need to make your interest visible. A quick 'haha' or a heart in the chat goes further than you'd think. Then say it in person: I'm not loud about it, but I really like you. I'd like this to be a relationship. Is that where you are? Byeong loves being told things. Tell them.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, a quick 'haha' keeps the sun shining. Cheap, effective.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, twelve texts to one reply is just Mu's exchange rate. Accept it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Count quality, not quantity. That one sentence was sincere.

jeong-fire.title: 'Yes, it was good' and the lantern rereading it
jeong-fire.text: A Jeong Fire brings warmth into your steady life, a lantern in the temple. They notice things, remember things, and send long messages about how a walk with you made them feel. You read them and feel good, and you reply 'it was a great day', and you mean every word. Here's what you might not see: Jeong can read your short reply again and again, looking for more underneath. The drift in this pair is a feelings gap. You don't flood people with emotion; Jeong needs some of it out loud. When Jeong is anxious about where this is going, you might say 'it's fine', and for you that's a complete reassurance. For Jeong, it can sound like you didn't hear the question. If Jeong goes quiet because something hurt, you may not notice until it's flaring. Your signal is reliability, and Jeong may not count it unless you name it. For the talk, add one feeling word. That's all. 'I'm happy with you' goes further than 'it's good'. Then say: I'd like us to be a couple, properly. When Jeong says something important, repeat it back so they know it landed. It feels odd. It works.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: A lantern in the mountain temple. Warm, quiet, lasting.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, 'it's fine' is not a reply to a paragraph.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: One sentence, repeated back. That's the whole repair.

mu-earth.title: Same table, same Thursday, no name
mu-earth.text: Two Mu Earths in a situationship are the most stable undefined thing in the world. You see each other every Thursday. You have a usual table at the dumpling place. You know how the other takes their tea. You have never once discussed what this is, and both of you seem completely fine with that. That's the drift for two mountains: it isn't vague, it's still. Nothing goes wrong, so nobody brings anything up. Both of you hide feelings behind 'it's fine', and both of you mean it, until one of you starts to want more and has no idea how to say so. Your texts are minimal and sincere: 'Home at 7.' 'Ok.' It works, and it also leaves no room for the big question. The other risk is stubbornness. If one of you finally raises it and the other hesitates, you might both dig in and leave it alone for months. For the talk, someone has to suggest change. Do it on a walk, side by side, which suits you both: I like what we have. I'd like it to be official. What do you think of that? Then send something unnecessary afterwards. A silly photo. Anything that isn't logistics.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Two mountains. Same table, same Thursday, same tea. Very safe.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And nobody's said what this is in four months. Classic.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Walk side by side. Say it to the path.

gi-earth.title: The invisible work in the valley
gi-earth.text: With a Gi Earth, you get mountain and valley, one landscape with two moods. Gi is soft where you're solid, attentive where you're steady. They ask how your day was, they remember your mother's name, they quietly sort things you didn't even notice needed sorting. You're comfortable together almost immediately. The drift in this situationship is the invisible work. Gi does a lot of it: checking in, planning, making things smooth. You reply with short, solid answers and assume that if something were wrong, Gi would say. Gi, meanwhile, assumes that if you cared, you'd ask. So Gi worries about what this is and you say 'don't worry about it', which, for Gi, is the least comforting sentence in English. If it ever comes out, it may arrive as 'I feel like I'm doing everything', and that could honestly surprise you. Your signal is calm, which can read as not noticing. For the talk, ask a question back for once. Several, actually. Then say: I know I'm not very expressive, but I'm serious about you. I want us to be a couple. Thank Gi, specifically, for one thing they've done that you never mentioned.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mountain and valley. One landscape, two moods.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, 'don't worry' has never helped a Gi in recorded history.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, say what you need before you're tired.

gyeong-metal.title: Decide tonight or sleep on it for a week
gyeong-metal.text: A Gyeong Metal is ore inside your mountain: strength protecting strength. You get each other. No drama, no games, no 47-message threads. Your texts are short on both sides, and it works. Mostly. The drift in this situationship is pace. Gyeong wants to decide things tonight. You want to sleep on it, possibly for a week. When Gyeong asks 'so what are we doing', it can feel like being rushed, and you go still. Gyeong reads stillness as stalling and gets blunter. The bluntness bruises you more than you show, and you dig in, and now two proud people are standing very close to each other, refusing to move first. Neither of you apologises easily, so small standoffs can last. Your signal is patience, which Gyeong can read as reluctance. For the talk, you don't have to answer instantly, but you do have to answer. Tell Gyeong your timing: Give me until Sunday, I want to think properly. Then on Sunday, say it: I'd like us to be together. I'm slow, not unsure. And add one personal line to your texts each day. Efficient is fine. Efficient with warmth is better.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Strength protecting strength. You two make a solid team.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong wants an answer tonight. Mu wants a week. Meet at Sunday.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Slow is not the same as unsure.

sin-metal.title: Eleven hints and a mountain that missed them
sin-metal.text: A Sin Metal is the gem your mountain wants to protect. Sin is sharp, elegant and a bit precious, and you find yourself wanting to look after them. Sin, in turn, seems to find your steadiness restful. It's a good match. It's also a match full of missed hints. The drift in this situationship happens through subtext. Sin hints. A comment about a friend whose partner planned a weekend away. A story post with a song that clearly means something. A cooler reply when you forgot to compliment the haircut. You miss all of it, not because you don't care but because you're a mountain and mountains take things at face value. Sin can feel unappreciated. You can feel like you're being graded on a test you never saw. Sin might also critique your simplicity, your same jacket, your same Thursday, and you might find Sin high-maintenance. Your signal is quiet devotion, which Sin needs to see out loud. For the talk, compliment specifically first. Not 'you look nice'. 'That green really suits you.' Then: I'd like us to be together, officially. Is that you too? And ask Sin, directly, if there's anything they've been hinting at.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The mountain guards the gem. Steady love, very safe.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin, Mu missed all eleven hints. Use words.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, compliment the green jacket. Specifically.

im-water.title: The dam, the river and the booked table
im-water.text: An Im Water is the river you can't quite stop watching. Big, clever, restless. They want to decide on the day, book flights at midnight, quit things on a whim. You admire it from your mountain, and it also makes you slightly nervous. The drift in this situationship is the dam and the river. You try to hold things in place: a regular night, a booked table, a plan for next month. Im can feel that as containment and push back, cancelling, changing, suggesting something else. You get frustrated by the shifting, Im gets bored by the routine, and both of you dig in. Money and plans become the battlefield: you'd rather save for something, Im would rather spend on an experience now. Under all that, the question of what this is gets lost. Your signal is consistency, which can feel to Im like a cage. For the talk, allow some irregularity, and say what you can't live without, clearly: I don't need us to plan everything. I just need to know this is real between us. Where are you on that? Then ask Im what freedom they need, and see if your mountain can make room for some of it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The dam and the river. Strong on both sides.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, keep one plan exactly as made. Just one.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, allow a little irregularity. The river needs to move.

gye-water.title: Mist, a poem and 'bring an umbrella'
gye-water.text: 戊 and 癸 form a heavenly combination: mist on the mountain. With a Gye Water, you feel a strange softness come over you. Gye is gentle, intuitive and a little mysterious, and you find yourself wanting to shelter them. Gye, in turn, seems drawn to your calm. The drift in this situationship is feelings versus facts. Gye shares a mood, a song, a sad thought about a film. You offer a plan, a solution, or a practical 'just get some sleep'. You meant care. Gye can feel dismissed, as if feelings were problems to be solved. Gye's moods also change faster than you're used to, and that can confuse you. You might start to see Gye as changeable, and Gye might start to see you as emotionally unavailable. Your protective instinct can also tip into managing, which Gye feels as being contained. Your signal is steadiness, which needs one feeling word to be recognised as love. For the talk, respond to the feeling first. If Gye says 'I've been anxious about us', say 'I'm glad you told me' before anything else. Then: I want to be with you. Properly. Is that what you'd like? Don't fix. Just hold.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: 戊癸, mist on the mountain. Gentle and rare.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, 'bring an umbrella' is not a reply to a poem.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, say it without the poem once.
